questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Shilpi has / a keen interest / of learning / a foreign language.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'of learning'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There is an error in **preposition usage **in the part *of learning.*
 
• **Of **is a preposition that is used for the following - 
 
 
• Of (to indicate relating to, belonging to) — *I always dreamed of being famous.*
 
• Of (to indicate reference) — *This is a picture of my last birthday.*
 
• Of (to specify the number or an amount) — *A good number of people understand Hindi.*
 
 
 
• None of the above usage points can be applied in the context of the given sentence. 
 
• So, option 2 is the correct answer as it contains the erroneous part *of learning.*
 
• The **correct preposition** in the context of the given sentence is **in** as it is used to indicate opinion, belief, feeling, etc.

**Correct sentence__ - ***Shilpi has / a keen interest / **in learning** / a foreign language.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.**

Kavya didn't wanted / any help / in painting.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'Kavya didn't wanted'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Didn't' is a contraction of 'did' and 'not'.
 
• **'Did' **is a **modal** and a modal is always followed by the **base form of a verb**.
 
• Hence, 'want' (base form) must replace 'wanted' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• So, **option 1 **is the correct answer. 

**Correct sentence__ - *****Kavya didn't want** / any help / in painting.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

His condition was so critical that a senior doctor ______ performed the operation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'himself'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• From the given options it is clear that we need to select the correct **pronoun **for the given blank that would refer to the senior doctor who performed the operation. 
 
• Let us look into the usage of the given **pronouns** in the options - 
 
 
• **yourself- **Used as a reflexive pronoun__ (*Did you hurt yourself?; Help yourself to some cake, Tim*) and __for emphasis__ (*You are going to have to do it yourself*).
 
• **myself - **Used as a __reflexive pronoun__ (*I restrained myself).*
 
• **itself - **Used as the __object of a verb or preposition __when it refers to something that is the same thing as the subject of the verb. (*Remarkable new evidence showing how the body rebuilds itself while we sleep.*)
 
• **himself - **Used to emphasize the person or thing that you are referring to. (*I heard this with my own ears from the President himself.*)
 
 
 
• From the above explanations, it is evident that **himself **is the the correct pronoun for the given blank. 
 
• Hence, **option 4 **is the correct answer. 

**__Correct sentence__ - ***His condition was so critical that a senior doctor __**himself**__** **performed the operation.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

Molly Yvonne didn't know what to do. She was torn apart **__with__** conflicting emotions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'by'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part **with **is a preposition. 
 
• We use **with **to show the tool or object used to do something** **- *I made this cake with the oven.*
 
• This cannot be applied in the given context. 
 
• We need to use the **preposition by **to identifying the agent performing an action. The subject (she) was torn apart **by **agent performing the action (conflicting emotions). 
 
• Hence, **option 4 **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence__ - ***Molly Yvonne didn't know what to do. She was torn apart **__by__ **conflicting emotions.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

The old man was __**too weak that he couldn't **__ climb the stairs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'too weak to'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• From the given options it is evident that we need to select the correct combination of prepositions and adverbs along with the adjective weak to replace the underlined segment. 
 
• Since **weak **is an **adjective **we need an **adverb **before it to modify it. 
 
• So, the phrase **so weak to** or **option 1 **is negated. 
 
• Both **very **and **too **are **adverbs. **
 
 
• **​Very **is used to emphasize that the following description applies without qualification.
 
• **Too **is used to show a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible; excessively.
 
• Thus, **too **is the best fit adverb to describe **weak **in the given context. 
 
 
 
• Hence the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is **too weak to.** 
 
• So, **option 4 **is the ***correct answer. ***

**Correct sentence__ - ***The old man was __**too weak to **__he couldn't climb the stairs.*

questions.question:
**The following sentences has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.**

Please let me know/ whether you decide/ to come with me.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'whether you decide'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the ***part, whether you decide*** lies in using the wrong tense. 
 
• **Decide **is the *simple present tense *form. 
 
• But the sentence implies that the decision has already been made and the subject wants to know about it. 
 
• In such a case we need to use the **present perfect tense form, *have decided. ***
 
• **Present Perfect Tense** is used to describe an action which is already completed (Perfect refers to a completed action) but which has a direct connection with the present or Place. (Hence the present prefix.)
 
• So, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 

**Correct sentence__** - *Please let me *know* **whether you have decided **to come with me.*
